scope: Corollary 2.5 (Three endpoint substitutions) of the manuscript “Posterior replicas and conditional information in Gaussian regression” (preprints/Posterior-replicas-and-conditional-information-in-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 135be898557ce66e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume 0 < ϵ ≤ 1/10 in Lemma 2.4. For sufficiently large d the following bounds hold. (i) If G is Gaussian, p ≥ 3/5, and 0 ≤ b ≤ d/2, the beta-variance bound (with the separate deterministic case at b = 0) and the angular cap just described give I(S; V | G, GS) ≥ 1 2(d − b − 1) log 1 5ϵ − log 2. (7) (ii) If G is a Haar frame, p ≥ 2/3, and b = ⌊d/4⌋, Markov’s bound P{R < 1/2} ≤ 4b/(3d) ≤ 1/3 gives I(S; V | G, GS) ≥ 1 3(d − b − 1) log 1 4ϵ − log 2. (8) (iii) If G is Gaussian, p ≥ 3/5, and b = ⌊d/2⌋, the direct Gaussian bound P{R < 1/2} ≤ 90/d gives I(S; V | G, GS) ≥ 1 2(d − b − 1) log 1 4ϵ − log 2. (9) Each right side is at least c d log(1/ϵ) for an absolute c > 0 and all sufficiently large d.
